newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes shade higher on data, grades steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes shade higher on data, grades steady.

text.p: U.S. crude prices strengthened Wednesday morning on the back of supportive stock draws as recorded in American Petroleum Institute (API) and Department of Energy data released the previous two days.
Grade barrels found differentials steady against the rising outright price, with only modest refiner interest in cleaning-up the last of June cash business.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing checked-in around five cents firmer at $21.60-70 a barrel. The June/July spread, or roll, narrowed from Tuesday to sell at -20 cents.
Domestic barrels saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James steady at flat to five cents under June WTI, while July barrels were talked at a discount of 10-6 cents.
Midland/WTI sold at WTI/Cushing -41 cents, steady from Tuesday, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire barely talked at a negative 65-60 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded hands at $1.50 under benchmark WTI, traders said. June Postings were also steady at $1.75, and talked out to $1.77.
Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) were sold to a 30 cents premium late Tuesday, and were pegged Wednesday at +22-26 cents.

Traders said expectations for foreign deliveries against the now expired June NYMEX contract spiked EFPs to firmer levels. Worries over off-spec crude deliveries have taken center stage among sectors of the market.
The game being played is to avoid getting stuck with foreign barrels, notably Nigerian Bonny Light, which demands a 60 cents premium payment from the receiving refiner.
"People being forced to take this stuff (Bonny Light) are claiming it doesn't meet specs, but it's really about money and the fact nobody wants it," said a cash dealer.
EFPs are the protection from having to take foreign barrels, allowing a buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for a physical position.
